msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Computer Vision > Image Analysis > Tags

questions.topic: Implement Knowledge Mining and Cognitive Search Solutions
questions.questionText: You are building an app that will include one million scanned magazine articles. Each article will be stored as an image file. You need to extract the text content from the images and then enable users to search for specific keywords within the articles. Which Azure service should you use to extract the text?
options: B. the Read API in Computer Vision
D. Azure Cognitive Service for Language
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. The Read API in Computer Vision.

The Read API (now part of Azure AI Vision) is specifically designed for extracting large amounts of text from images and documents. It handles both printed and handwritten text, works well with multi-page documents and large volumes of content, and uses asynchronous processing that scales well for one million articles. It is the recommended OCR solution for text-heavy documents.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Computer Vision Image Analysis has an OCR feature, but the Read API is the recommended and more capable solution for extracting text from document images at scale.
- C. Form Recognizer (Document Intelligence) is optimized for extracting structured data from forms, invoices, and receipts. For general text extraction from magazine articles (unstructured text), the Read API is more appropriate.
- D. Azure Cognitive Service for Language processes text that has already been extracted. It cannot extract text from images.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Vision Read API large scale OCR
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Computer Vision > Read API
searchKeywords: Read API OCR large document volume

questions.questionText:
You are building an app that will share user images. You need to configure the app to perform the following actions when users upload images:
- Identify images that contain known brands or logos
- Generate descriptive tags for the image content

Which Azure AI service feature should you use?
options: A. object detection in Azure AI Computer Vision
B. content tags in Azure AI Computer Vision
C. image descriptions in Azure AI Computer Vision
D. image type detection in Azure AI Computer Vision
E. image classification in Azure AI Custom Vision
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Content tags in Azure AI Computer Vision.

The tagging feature in Azure AI Computer Vision can identify a wide range of content in images, including objects, actions, scenery, and brand logos. It generates descriptive tags with confidence scores. The tag feature includes brand detection capabilities, which can identify commercial logos and brands in images.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Object detection identifies and locates objects with bounding boxes, but brand/logo detection is part of the analysis/tagging feature, not object detection.
- C. Image descriptions generate natural language captions for images but do not specifically identify brands or logos.
- D. Image type detection determines whether an image is clip art or a line drawing. It does not identify brands or generate content tags.
- E. Custom Vision image classification requires training a custom model. The built-in Computer Vision tagging feature already includes brand detection without custom training.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Vision content tags brand detection
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Computer Vision > Image Analysis > Brands

questions.questionText: You are building an app that will use the Azure AI Video Indexer service. You plan to train a language model to recognize industry-specific terminology. Which file format should you use to provide training data for the language model?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. TXT.

Azure AI Video Indexer accepts plain text (.txt) files for training custom language models. The text file should contain examples of the industry-specific terminology and phrases you want the model to recognize during speech-to-text transcription.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. XML is not a supported file format for Video Indexer language model training data.
- C. XLS (Excel) is not a supported file format for Video Indexer language model training data.
- D. PDF is not a supported file format for Video Indexer language model training data.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Video Indexer custom language model TXT
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Computer Vision > Video Indexer > Customize models

questions.questionText: You are developing a method that uses the Azure AI Vision client library. The method will perform optical character recognition (OCR) on an image. You have the following code that calls the Read API, but the results are always empty. What should you do to fix the issue?
options: B. Add code to verify the read_results.status value.
C. Add code to verify the status of the read_operation_location value.
D. Wrap the call to get_read_result within a loop that contains a delay.
questions.explanation:
Correct: D. Wrap the call to get_read_result within a loop that contains a delay.

The Read API in Azure AI Vision operates asynchronously. When you submit an image for OCR, the service returns an operation ID immediately while processing continues in the background. You must poll the get_read_result endpoint with the operation ID and wait until the operation status is 'succeeded' before reading the results. Without a polling loop with delays, you may retrieve the results before processing is complete, which is why the results are always empty.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. The operation_id parameter is required to retrieve the results of the asynchronous read operation. Removing it would cause an error.
- B. Verifying the status value is part of the solution but insufficient on its own. You need the polling loop to keep checking until the status changes to 'succeeded'.
- C. The read_operation_location contains the URL for polling. Verifying it alone does not solve the timing issue of reading results before processing completes.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Vision Read API async polling loop
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Computer Vision > Read API > How-to

questions.questionText: You are building a Conversational Language Understanding model for an e-commerce chatbot. Users can speak or type their requests for products. Some product names are complex and can vary significantly. You need to choose the correct entity type that will capture any product name mentioned by the user. Which entity type should you use?
questions.explanation:
Correct: A. Learned.

A learned (machine-learned) entity in Conversational Language Understanding (CLU) is trained from labeled examples and can extract entities from context. This is the best choice for product names that vary significantly, as the model learns to identify product names from the surrounding context in user utterances without requiring an exhaustive predefined list.

Why the others are wrong:
- B. Regex entities match patterns defined by regular expressions. Product names do not follow consistent patterns that can be captured by regex.
- C. List entities match against a predefined list of values. Since product names are complex and vary significantly, maintaining a comprehensive list would be impractical.
- D. Pattern.any is a LUIS concept that captures entities of variable length in template utterances. In CLU, learned entities are the preferred approach for flexible entity extraction.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Language CLU learned machine-learned entities
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Language Service > CLU > Entities

questions.questionText: You are building an Azure WebJob that will create knowledge bases from an array of URLs. You instantiate a QnAMakerClient object. Which two actions should you perform in sequence to create a knowledge base?
options: A. Create a list of FileDTO objects that represents data from the WebJob.
C. Create a list of QnADTO objects that represents data from the WebJob.
questions.explanation:
Correct: D. Create a CreateKbDTO object, then B. Call the client.Knowledgebase.CreateAsync method.

To create a knowledge base using the QnA Maker SDK:
1. First, create a CreateKbDTO object that contains the knowledge base configuration, including the name and the list of URLs to extract QnA pairs from.
2. Then, call client.Knowledgebase.CreateAsync with the CreateKbDTO object to create the knowledge base.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. FileDTO objects represent files to upload, but the scenario specifies URLs as the data source. The URLs are specified in the CreateKbDTO object.
- C. QnADTO objects represent individual question-answer pairs for manual entry. Since the knowledge base is being created from URLs, the service automatically extracts QnA pairs from the web pages.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Language QnA Maker knowledge base SDK
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Language Service > Question answering > SDK

questions.questionText: You are developing an application that includes language translation. The application will translate text retrieved by user queries. You need to determine the sentiment of the translated text for analytics. Which feature should you enable on the prediction endpoint?
options: A. Add show-all-intents=true to the prediction endpoint query.
C. Add log=true to the prediction endpoint query.
questions.explanation:
Correct: D. Enable sentiment analysis.

To determine the sentiment of text, you need to enable sentiment analysis. In Azure AI Language and LUIS, sentiment analysis can be enabled on the prediction endpoint to return sentiment scores (positive, neutral, negative) alongside the regular predictions. This provides the analytics data needed.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. show-all-intents=true returns confidence scores for all intents rather than just the top intent. It does not provide sentiment information.
- B. Speech priming optimizes speech recognition by using LUIS app context. It is not related to sentiment analysis.
- C. log=true enables logging of endpoint queries for active learning purposes. It does not perform sentiment analysis on the text.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Language sentiment analysis on prediction
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Language Service > Sentiment analysis

questions.questionText: You are developing a method for an application that uses the Translator API. The method will receive the content of a web page written in Greek and translate the text to English while also transliterating the Greek text to Latin script. Which two parameters must you include in the API request?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C. textType=html and F. toScript=Latn.

textType=html: Since the content comes from a web page, it contains HTML markup. Setting textType=html tells the Translator API to handle HTML tags properly, preserving the markup while translating only the text content.

toScript=Latn: This parameter specifies that the output should be transliterated to Latin script. Since the requirement is to transliterate Greek text to Latin script, toScript=Latn is the correct value.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. toScript=Cyrl would transliterate to Cyrillic script, not Latin script.
- B. from=el specifies Greek as the source language, but the Translator API auto-detects the source language, so this is not strictly required. The question asks for the must-include parameters.
- D. to=el would set Greek as the target translation language, but the requirement is to translate to English (to=en).
- E. textType=plain would treat HTML tags as plain text, corrupting the web page content.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Translator HTML transliteration
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Translator > Reference > Translate

questions.questionText: You have a chatbot that was built by using the Microsoft Bot Framework. You need to debug the chatbot endpoint remotely. Which two tools should you use together?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C. Bot Framework Emulator and E. ngrok.

To debug a chatbot endpoint remotely:
- Bot Framework Emulator: A desktop application that allows you to test and debug bots. It can connect to bots running locally or remotely and provides inspection of messages, activity logs, and JSON data.
- ngrok: A tunneling tool that creates a secure tunnel from the public internet to your local machine. When combined with the Bot Framework Emulator, ngrok enables remote debugging by exposing your locally-running bot to the internet so that channels and services can reach it.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Fiddler is a web debugging proxy for capturing HTTP traffic, but it is not specifically designed for Bot Framework debugging.
- B. Bot Framework Composer is a visual authoring tool for building bots, not a debugging tool for remote endpoints.
- D. Bot Framework CLI provides command-line tools for managing bot resources, not for interactive debugging.
- F. nginx is a web server and reverse proxy. It is not a bot debugging tool.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure Bot Service debugging with ngrok emulator
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > Bot Service > Develop > Debug
msLearn.lookFor: Debug a bot using the Bot Framework Emulator

questions.questionText:
Note: This question is part of a series of questions that present the same scenario. Each question in the series contains a unique solution that might meet the stated goal.

You have a Language Understanding resource. A conversational expert provides you with the following list of phrases to use for training:
- Find a pharmacy
- Where is the nearest coffee shop?
- Get directions to the airport
- How do I get to the grocery store?

You need to create a new intent and add the phrases as example utterances.

Solution: You create an intent named 'FindLocation' and add all four phrases as utterances.

Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Correct: A. Yes.

All four phrases express the same general intent of finding a location or getting directions to a place. Creating a single intent named 'FindLocation' and adding all four phrases as example utterances is the correct approach. The phrases represent variations of the same user intent, which helps the Language Understanding model learn to recognize different ways users might express this intent.

The intent name 'FindLocation' is descriptive and appropriate. Adding multiple varied utterances improves the model's ability to generalize and correctly classify new, similar phrases.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Language CLU intents training utterances
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Language Service > CLU > Build model

questions.questionText: You need to measure the public perception of your brand on social media by using natural language processing. Which Azure AI service should you use?
questions.explanation:
Correct: A. Language service.

Azure AI Language service includes sentiment analysis, which can analyze social media text to determine whether the sentiment is positive, negative, neutral, or mixed. This directly measures public perception of your brand. The Language service also offers opinion mining, which can identify specific aspects and the sentiment toward them.

Why the others are wrong:
- B. Content Moderator is designed to detect potentially offensive, risky, or unwanted content. It does not measure brand perception or sentiment.
- C. Computer Vision analyzes images and videos, not text content from social media posts. It cannot perform sentiment analysis.
- D. Form Recognizer (Document Intelligence) extracts structured data from forms and documents. It has no natural language understanding or sentiment analysis capabilities.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Language sentiment analysis social media
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Language Service > Sentiment analysis

questions.questionText: You are building a call handling system that will receive calls from French-speaking and German-speaking callers. The system must transcribe the speech to text and then synthesize text responses back to speech. You need to identify the correct API endpoints. Which endpoints should you use for speech-to-text and text-to-speech?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B for speech-to-text and D for text-to-speech.

B. https://uksouth.stt.speech.microsoft.com/speech/recognition/conversation/cognitiveservices/v1 is the speech-to-text REST API endpoint for real-time speech recognition. This endpoint accepts audio input and returns transcribed text.

D. https://uksouth.tts.speech.microsoft.com/cognitiveservices/v1 is the text-to-speech REST API endpoint that accepts SSML input and returns synthesized audio output.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. This endpoint is for managing custom speech models (listing base models), not for performing speech-to-text transcription.
- C. This endpoint retrieves the list of available voices for text-to-speech. It does not perform speech synthesis.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Speech REST API endpoints STT TTS
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Speech Service > Reference > REST API

questions.questionText: You develop a custom question answering project in Azure Cognitive Service for Language. The project will be used by a customer support team. Users report that the system does not return answers when questions are phrased differently from the source material. You need to improve the match rate without adding new content. What should you do?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C. Add alternate questions.

Adding alternate questions (also known as alternative phrasing) to existing QnA pairs increases the number of ways a question can be matched. When users phrase questions differently from the source material, having alternate phrasings helps the system match the user's query to the correct answer. This directly addresses the problem without adding new content.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Follow-up prompts create multi-turn conversations by suggesting related questions after an answer. They do not improve the initial matching of differently-phrased questions.
- B. Active learning suggests potential alternate questions based on user queries, but it requires ongoing user traffic and manual review. Adding alternate questions directly is more immediate and targeted.
- D. Chit-chat adds pre-built conversational personality responses (greetings, small talk). It does not improve matching for domain-specific questions.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Language question answering alternate questions
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Language Service > Question answering > Improve model

questions.topic: Implement Knowledge Mining and Cognitive Search Solutions
questions.questionText: You deploy a web app that is used as a management portal for indexing in Azure Cognitive Search. The app is configured to use the primary admin key of the search service. You discover that the primary admin key has been compromised. You need to mitigate the security risk while ensuring the app continues to function. What should you do?
options: A. Regenerate the primary admin key, change the app to use the secondary admin key, and then regenerate the secondary admin key.
B. Change the app to use a query key, and then regenerate the primary admin key and the secondary admin key.
C. Regenerate the secondary admin key, change the app to use the secondary admin key, and then regenerate the primary admin key.
D. Add a new query key, change the app to use the new query key, and then delete all the unused query keys.
questions.explanation:
Correct: C. Regenerate the secondary admin key, change the app to use the secondary admin key, and then regenerate the primary admin key.

This is the correct sequence to mitigate the compromised primary admin key while keeping the app functional:
1. First, regenerate the secondary admin key to get a fresh, uncompromised key.
2. Update the app to use the new secondary admin key. This ensures continuity since the app is a management portal that needs admin-level access for indexing operations.
3. Finally, regenerate the primary admin key to invalidate the compromised key.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Regenerating the primary admin key first would immediately break the app since it is currently using that key. The app would experience downtime.
- B. Query keys only provide read access for searching. The app is a management portal for indexing, which requires admin-level access (write operations). A query key would not be sufficient.
- D. Similar to B, query keys provide read-only access and cannot perform indexing management operations that the app requires.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Search admin key security rotation
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Search > Security > Manage API keys

questions.questionText: You are building an application that uses Azure OpenAI Service. You need to limit the number of tokens generated in a completion response to control costs. Which parameter should you configure in the API request?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. The max_tokens parameter controls the maximum number of tokens the model will generate in the completion response. Setting this value limits the response length and helps control costs since Azure OpenAI charges per token.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. temperature controls the randomness/creativity of the output (0 = deterministic, higher = more random) but does not limit the length of the response.
- C. top_p (nucleus sampling) controls the diversity of the response by limiting the cumulative probability of token selections. It affects quality, not length.
- D. frequency_penalty reduces the likelihood of the model repeating the same tokens. It affects repetition, not the maximum output length.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure OpenAI max_tokens completion parameter
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Azure OpenAI > Reference > Completions

questions.questionText: You are developing a chatbot using Azure OpenAI Service with the GPT-4 model. You need to provide the model with a system-level instruction that defines the chatbot's persona and behavior throughout the conversation. Which message role should you use?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C. The system message role is used to provide high-level instructions that define the AI assistant's behavior, persona, and constraints. It is set at the beginning of the conversation and guides the model's responses throughout.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. The user role represents messages from the end user asking questions or providing input. It is not used for defining the chatbot's behavior.
- B. The assistant role represents the model's own responses. It is not used for setting instructions but rather for including prior assistant responses in the conversation history.
- D. The function role is used in function calling scenarios to return the result of a function call back to the model. It is not for defining persona instructions.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure OpenAI Chat Completions system message role
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Azure OpenAI > How-to > Chat Completions

questions.questionText: You are building an Azure AI Search solution that indexes PDF documents stored in Azure Blob Storage. You need to enrich the index with key phrases extracted from the document content. Which component should you add to the indexer pipeline?
options: B. A skillset with a Key Phrase Extraction skill
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. A skillset with a Key Phrase Extraction cognitive skill is the correct approach. Skillsets are attached to indexers and define AI enrichment steps. The Key Phrase Extraction skill uses Azure AI Language to extract key phrases from document content during indexing.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. A custom analyzer defines how text is tokenized and filtered during indexing and querying (e.g., for language-specific analysis). It does not extract key phrases from content.
- C. A synonym map maps terms to their synonyms to improve search recall. It does not extract key phrases from documents.
- D. A scoring profile defines rules for boosting search results based on field values or freshness. It affects relevance scoring, not content enrichment.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Search key phrase extraction skillset
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Search > Cognitive search > Key phrase extraction skill
searchKeywords: AI Search key phrase extraction skillset

questions.questionText: You are building a customer feedback analysis system. You need to determine not just the overall sentiment of each review but also identify sentiment toward specific aspects such as 'food quality' and 'service speed'. Which Azure AI Language feature should you use?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Opinion Mining (also called Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis) identifies specific aspects (targets) mentioned in text and the sentiment associated with each aspect. For example, it can determine that 'food quality' has positive sentiment while 'service speed' has negative sentiment in the same review.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Standard Sentiment Analysis provides an overall sentiment score for the entire text (positive, negative, neutral, mixed) but does not break it down by specific aspects or targets.
- C. Key Phrase Extraction identifies important phrases in the text but does not associate sentiment with those phrases.
- D. Named Entity Recognition identifies and categorizes entities (people, organizations, locations) but does not analyze sentiment toward those entities.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Language opinion mining aspect-based sentiment
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Language Service > Opinion mining

questions.questionText: You are implementing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pattern using Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Search. Which TWO components are essential for this pattern? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
options: A. An Azure AI Search index containing your organization's documents
B. A fine-tuned Azure OpenAI model trained on your data
C. An orchestration layer that retrieves relevant documents and includes them in the prompt
D. A custom neural voice profile for the responses
questions.explanation:
Correct: A and C. The RAG pattern requires (A) a search index containing your organization's knowledge base documents so that relevant content can be retrieved, and (C) an orchestration layer that queries the search index based on the user's question, retrieves relevant documents, and includes them as context in the prompt sent to the Azure OpenAI model.

Why the others are wrong:
- B. Fine-tuning the model on your data is a different approach from RAG. RAG specifically avoids the need for fine-tuning by providing relevant documents as context at query time. Fine-tuning changes model weights, while RAG augments the prompt.
- D. A custom neural voice profile is related to Azure AI Speech text-to-speech capabilities. It is completely unrelated to the RAG pattern, which deals with grounding text generation in retrieved documents.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure OpenAI Retrieval Augmented Generation RAG
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Azure OpenAI > Concepts > Retrieval augmented generation

questions.questionText: You need to extract data from invoices that have a consistent layout unique to your organization. The prebuilt invoice model does not capture all the fields you need. What should you do?
options: A. Use the prebuilt Read model
B. Train a custom extraction model with labeled training data
C. Use the prebuilt General Document model
D. Use the Layout model with table extraction
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. When the prebuilt models do not capture all the fields you need, you should train a custom extraction model using labeled training data. Custom models allow you to define exactly which fields to extract based on your specific document layout, giving you full control over the extraction results.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. The Read model extracts text and layout information (OCR) but does not extract structured key-value pairs or custom fields. It returns raw text without understanding document structure.
- C. The General Document model extracts key-value pairs, entities, and tables from documents, but it uses a generic approach and may not capture organization-specific fields reliably.
- D. The Layout model extracts text, tables, and selection marks but does not extract custom key-value fields specific to your invoice format.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Document Intelligence custom extraction model
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Document Intelligence > Custom models > Train model

questions.questionText: You are building a retail application that needs to detect specific products on store shelves using images. You have a dataset of labeled product images. Which Azure AI service should you use?
options: A. Azure AI Vision Image Analysis
B. Azure AI Custom Vision with object detection
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Azure AI Custom Vision with object detection allows you to train a model on your labeled product images to detect and locate specific products within images. Object detection provides bounding boxes around detected objects, which is ideal for identifying products on store shelves.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Azure AI Vision Image Analysis provides general image analysis including tagging and object detection with predefined categories, but it cannot be trained to recognize specific custom products unique to your retail application.
- C. Azure AI Face is specifically designed for face detection, recognition, and analysis. It cannot detect products or non-face objects.
- D. Azure AI Video Indexer is for analyzing video content to extract insights like spoken words, faces, and scenes. It is not designed for detecting specific products in still images.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Custom Vision object detection
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Custom Vision > Object detection

questions.questionText: You are building a voice-enabled application that needs to convert spoken English into text in real-time. The application must handle continuous speech and provide interim results as the user speaks. Which Azure AI Speech feature should you use?
options: C. Real-time Speech-to-Text with continuous recognition
questions.explanation:
Correct: C. Real-time Speech-to-Text with continuous recognition processes audio as it is received and provides both interim (partial) results and final recognized text. Continuous recognition keeps the recognition session open for ongoing speech, which is ideal for voice-enabled applications.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Speech Translation converts speech from one language to text or speech in another language. Since the requirement is English speech to English text (same language), translation is not needed.
- B. Batch Transcription is designed for transcribing large volumes of pre-recorded audio files asynchronously. It does not provide real-time or interim results.
- D. Speaker Recognition identifies who is speaking (verification or identification) but does not transcribe speech to text.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Speech continuous recognition real-time
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Speech Service > Speech-to-text > How-to

questions.questionText: You are building a Conversational Language Understanding (CLU) model for a virtual assistant. Users can ask 'Book a flight from Seattle to London on March 15'. You need to extract 'Seattle' as the departure city, 'London' as the destination city, and 'March 15' as the travel date. What should you define in your CLU model?
options: A. Three separate intents for each piece of information
B. Entities for departure city, destination city, and travel date
C. Three separate utterances with no entity labels
D. A synonym list for city names
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Entities are used to extract specific pieces of information from user utterances. You define entities for departure city, destination city, and travel date, and label them in your training utterances so the model learns to extract these values from new user inputs.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Intents represent the overall purpose of the user's request (e.g., 'BookFlight'). Creating separate intents for each piece of information would fragment the user's single request into multiple intents, which is incorrect. The entire utterance should map to a single 'BookFlight' intent with entities for the details.
- C. Utterances without entity labels would only help the model recognize the intent but would not teach it to extract the specific departure city, destination city, or travel date values.
- D. A synonym list helps map different terms to the same concept but does not enable extraction of contextual roles like departure vs. destination city from a single utterance.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Language CLU entity extraction training
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Language Service > CLU > Label data

questions.questionText: You are using Azure OpenAI Service and need to prevent the model from generating harmful or inappropriate content. Which feature should you enable?
options: B. Azure AI Content Safety filters
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Azure AI Content Safety filters are built into Azure OpenAI Service and can be configured to detect and block harmful content categories including hate, sexual, violence, and self-harm content in both prompts and completions. These filters can be set to different severity levels.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Token rate limiting controls how many tokens per minute can be processed to manage throughput and costs. It does not filter or moderate content for safety.
- C. Model fine-tuning with RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) is a training technique used to align models. It is not a configurable feature you enable on Azure OpenAI deployments to filter content at runtime.
- D. Prompt caching is a performance optimization that stores and reuses responses for identical prompts. It has no content moderation capability.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure OpenAI content safety content filters
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Azure OpenAI > Concepts > Content filtering

questions.questionText: You have an Azure AI Search index with a large number of documents. You need to implement semantic ranking to improve the relevance of search results by understanding the meaning of queries. What should you configure?
options: A. A scoring profile with term frequency boosting
B. A semantic configuration on the index
C. A custom analyzer with n-gram tokenization
D. A synonym map for the search fields
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. A semantic configuration on the index enables semantic ranking, which uses deep learning models to re-rank search results based on the semantic meaning of the query and documents. You define which fields should be used for semantic ranking in the configuration.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. A scoring profile with term frequency boosting uses traditional information retrieval techniques (BM25-based) to boost results based on term frequency. It does not understand semantic meaning.
- C. A custom analyzer with n-gram tokenization affects how text is tokenized during indexing and querying. N-grams help with partial matching but do not provide semantic understanding.
- D. A synonym map maps terms to their synonyms (e.g., 'car' to 'automobile') to improve recall. While useful, it does not provide the deep semantic understanding that semantic ranking offers.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Search semantic ranking configuration
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Search > Semantic search > How-to

questions.questionText: You have built a chatbot using the Microsoft Bot Framework and deployed it to Azure Bot Service. You need to make the bot available on Microsoft Teams and a company website. What should you configure?
options: A. Two separate bot registrations, one for each platform
B. Channels for Microsoft Teams and Web Chat in the bot resource
C. Two separate Azure App Service plans
D. A custom domain for each platform
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Azure Bot Service uses channels to connect a single bot to multiple communication platforms. You configure the Microsoft Teams channel and the Web Chat channel in the bot resource settings. Each channel adapter handles the platform-specific protocol translation.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. You do not need separate bot registrations. A single Azure Bot Service resource can connect to multiple channels simultaneously, which is one of its key benefits.
- C. Azure App Service plans host the bot's web application code. The number of platforms the bot connects to does not require separate hosting plans.
- D. Custom domains are related to DNS configuration for web endpoints. They are not the mechanism for making a bot available on different communication platforms like Teams.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure Bot Service channels Teams and Web Chat
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > Bot Service > Channels > Add channels

questions.questionText: You are building a custom text classification model using Azure AI Language. Which TWO steps are required to train the model? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
options: A. Label your training data with the appropriate class categories
B. Deploy the model to an Azure Kubernetes Service cluster
C. Define the classes and upload training documents to the Language resource
D. Configure a custom neural voice profile
questions.explanation:
Correct: A and C. To train a custom text classification model, you must (C) define your classification classes and upload training documents to your Language resource project, and (A) label the training documents with the appropriate class categories so the model can learn the association between text content and class labels.

Why the others are wrong:
- B. Deploying to Azure Kubernetes Service is not required for training. Once trained, the model is deployed to a deployment name within the Language resource itself. AKS deployment is not part of the custom text classification workflow.
- D. A custom neural voice profile is part of Azure AI Speech for creating custom text-to-speech voices. It is completely unrelated to text classification.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Language custom text classification training
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Language Service > Custom text classification > Train

questions.questionText: You are using the Azure OpenAI Embeddings API to create vector representations of documents for semantic search. Which model should you use?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. text-embedding-ada-002 is an embedding model specifically designed to generate vector representations (embeddings) of text. These embeddings capture the semantic meaning of text and can be used for semantic search, clustering, and similarity comparisons.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. gpt-4 is a large language model designed for text generation and conversation. While it processes text, it is not optimized for generating embeddings and is significantly more expensive for this purpose.
- C. dall-e-3 is an image generation model that creates images from text descriptions. It does not produce text embeddings.
- D. whisper is a speech-to-text model for audio transcription. It does not generate text embeddings.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure OpenAI embeddings text-embedding-ada-002
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Azure OpenAI > Concepts > Embeddings

questions.questionText: You are implementing vector search in Azure AI Search to enable semantic similarity search over your document collection. What must you configure on the index field that will store the vector embeddings?
options: A. Set the field type to Edm.String and enable filtering
B. Set the field type to Collection(Edm.Single) and configure a vector search profile
C. Set the field type to Edm.Int32 and enable sorting
D. Set the field type to Edm.GeographyPoint and enable faceting
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Vector fields in Azure AI Search use the type Collection(Edm.Single) to store arrays of floating-point numbers (the embedding vectors). You must also configure a vector search profile that specifies the algorithm (e.g., HNSW) and its parameters for approximate nearest neighbor search.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Edm.String is for text fields. Vector embeddings are numerical arrays, not strings. Filtering is a text/value-based operation, not a vector similarity operation.
- C. Edm.Int32 is for integer values. Embeddings are floating-point arrays, and sorting is irrelevant for vector similarity search.
- D. Edm.GeographyPoint is for geographic coordinates (latitude/longitude). It has nothing to do with vector embeddings, and faceting is for categorical aggregation.

questions.questionText: You are building a solution that needs to generate descriptive alt-text for images on a website to improve accessibility. Which Azure AI Vision capability should you use?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Image Captioning (Describe Image) generates human-readable descriptions of images in natural language. This is ideal for creating alt-text for accessibility because it produces complete sentences describing what is in the image.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Object Detection identifies and locates specific objects with bounding boxes. While it tells you what objects are in an image, it does not generate natural language descriptions suitable for alt-text.
- C. OCR (Read API) extracts text that appears within images. It does not describe the visual content of images, only reads any text present in them.
- D. Spatial Analysis analyzes the movement and presence of people in video feeds (e.g., counting people in an area). It is a video-based solution, not for generating image descriptions.

questions.questionText: You are using Azure OpenAI with the Chat Completions API. Your application needs to call external functions based on the model's output, such as looking up customer order status from a database. Which feature should you use?
options: A. Prompt engineering with few-shot examples
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Function calling allows the model to generate structured JSON output that specifies which function to call and with what arguments, based on the user's input. Your application can then execute the function (e.g., database lookup) and return the results to the model for a final response.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Prompt engineering with few-shot examples can help the model understand the desired format but does not provide a structured mechanism for the model to reliably specify function calls with typed parameters.
- C. Fine-tuning changes the model's weights based on training data. It does not provide a mechanism for real-time function calling or integration with external systems.
- D. Increasing the temperature makes the output more random and creative. This would actually make function calling less reliable, not enable it.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure OpenAI function calling external API
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Azure OpenAI > How-to > Function calling

questions.questionText: You are building an application that needs to translate spoken French into spoken German in real-time. Which TWO Azure AI Speech features do you need? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
questions.explanation:
Correct: B and C. Speech Translation (B) takes spoken input in one language and can output translated text. To produce spoken output in German, you also need Text-to-Speech (C) to synthesize the translated text into spoken German audio. Together, these features enable real-time speech-to-speech translation.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Speech-to-Text converts speech to text in the same language. Speech Translation already handles the speech input recognition and translation in one step, so a separate Speech-to-Text service is redundant.
- D. Speaker Recognition identifies or verifies who is speaking. It does not translate or synthesize speech.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure AI Speech Translation and TTS pipeline
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Speech Service > Speech translation

questions.questionText: You deploy an Azure AI Services multi-service resource. You need to authenticate API requests using Azure Active Directory (Entra ID) instead of subscription keys. What should you do?
options: A. Enable managed identity on the AI Services resource and assign the Cognitive Services User role to the calling application
B. Regenerate the subscription keys and store them in Azure Key Vault
C. Configure a virtual network service endpoint for the AI Services resource
D. Create a custom domain name for the AI Services resource
questions.explanation:
Correct: A. To use Azure AD (Entra ID) authentication with Azure AI Services, you need to use role-based access control (RBAC). You assign the Cognitive Services User role (or similar role) to the managed identity or service principal of the calling application. The application then obtains an Azure AD token to authenticate API requests.

Why the others are wrong:
- B. Storing keys in Key Vault is a security best practice for key management but still uses key-based authentication, not Azure AD authentication.
- C. Virtual network service endpoints restrict network access to the AI Services resource. They control which networks can reach the endpoint but do not change the authentication method.
- D. A custom domain name is required for some Azure AD authentication scenarios with containers, but creating a custom domain alone does not configure Azure AD authentication.

questions.questionText: You are building a knowledge mining solution using Azure AI Search with an indexer that processes documents from Azure Blob Storage. The indexer enriches documents using a skillset. Which TWO outputs can a knowledge store projection generate? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
options: A. Tables in Azure Table Storage
B. Queues in Azure Queue Storage
C. Blobs (JSON or image files) in Azure Blob Storage
D. Topics in Azure Service Bus
questions.explanation:
Correct: A and C. A knowledge store in Azure AI Search supports three types of projections: table projections that store structured data in Azure Table Storage (A), object projections that store JSON documents in Azure Blob Storage, and file projections that store extracted images in Azure Blob Storage (C).

Why the others are wrong:
- B. Azure Queue Storage is a messaging service for asynchronous communication. Knowledge store projections do not write to queues.
- D. Azure Service Bus topics are for publish-subscribe messaging patterns. Knowledge store projections do not output to Service Bus.

questions.questionText: You need to deploy an Azure OpenAI model that will handle a high volume of requests. You want to ensure consistent throughput without per-call throttling. Which deployment type should you use?
options: A. Standard deployment with pay-per-token pricing
C. A batch deployment for offline processing
D. A development deployment with free tier
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Provisioned Throughput Units (PTU) deployment provides reserved model processing capacity measured in throughput units. This guarantees consistent throughput without being subject to per-call token-per-minute rate limits, making it ideal for high-volume production workloads.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Standard deployment with pay-per-token pricing is subject to token-per-minute rate limits that can cause throttling under high load. It is suitable for variable or lower-volume workloads.
- C. Batch deployments process requests asynchronously in bulk. They are designed for offline processing of large datasets, not for real-time high-throughput API serving.
- D. There is no specific 'development deployment with free tier' in Azure OpenAI. Standard deployments have rate limits, and all deployments incur costs based on usage or provisioned capacity.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Azure OpenAI provisioned throughput PTU deployment
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Azure OpenAI > Concepts > Provisioned throughput

questions.questionText: You are designing an AI solution that will process personal data of EU citizens. According to responsible AI principles, what must you ensure regarding data handling?
options: A. All data must be stored in a US-based data center for optimal performance
B. Users must be informed about how their data is collected, used, and stored, and must provide consent
C. Personal data should be retained indefinitely to improve model accuracy over time
D. Data processing details should be kept confidential to protect intellectual property
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Responsible AI principles require transparency about data handling and user consent. Users must be informed about how their personal data is collected, used, and stored. This aligns with both the Transparency principle of responsible AI and privacy regulations like GDPR.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Data residency requirements, especially for EU citizens under GDPR, may require data to be stored in the EU. Storing data in the US without appropriate safeguards could violate data protection regulations.
- C. Retaining personal data indefinitely violates the data minimization principle. Data should be retained only as long as necessary for its stated purpose.
- D. Keeping data processing details confidential from users contradicts the Transparency principle. Users have the right to understand how their data is processed.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Responsible AI privacy user consent GDPR
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Services > Responsible use of AI > Overview

questions.questionText:
You have an Azure subscription that contains an Azure OpenAI resource named AI1 and a user named User1.

You need to ensure that User1 can perform the following actions in Azure OpenAI Studio:

- Identify resource endpoints.
- View models that are available for deployment.
- Generate text and images by using the deployed models.

Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Cognitive Services OpenAI User. This role grants the ability to use the Azure OpenAI service including viewing endpoints, listing available models, and making inference calls (generating text and images). This is the least-privilege role satisfying all three requirements. B. Cognitive Services Contributor grants management-plane permissions exceeding least privilege. C. Contributor is a broad role far exceeding least privilege. D. Cognitive Services OpenAI Contributor grants additional permissions to create deployments and fine-tune models, more than needed for simply using deployed models.

questions.questionText: You are developing an extract solution for receipt images. The solution must trigger a manual review when extracted information falls below a confidence threshold of 70 percent. You upload receipt images to the Form Recognizer API for analysis and the API returns JSON results. Which expression should you use to trigger a manual review of the extracted information?
questions.explanation: Correct: B. documentResults.fields.*.confidence < 0.7. This expression evaluates confidence scores for ALL extracted fields using the wildcard (*). Since the requirement is that any confidence below 70% (0.7) triggers human review, the wildcard ensures manual review is triggered if any field confidence is below the threshold. A. This checks document type, not confidence scores. C. This checks if ReceiptType confidence is GREATER than 0.7, which would trigger review when confidence is high - the opposite of what is needed. D. This checks only MerchantName field confidence, not all fields.

questions.questionText: You are developing the smart e-commerce project for Wide World Importers. You need to implement autocompletion as part of the Cognitive Search solution to support autocompletion and suggestion based on all product name variants. Which three actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
options: A. Make API queries to the autocomplete endpoint and include suggesterName in the body.
B. Add a suggester that has the three product name fields as source fields.
C. Make API queries to the search endpoint and include the product name fields in the searchFields query parameter.
D. Add a suggester for each of the three product name fields.
E. Set the searchAnalyzer property for the three product name variants.
F. Set the analyzer property for the three product name variants.
questions.explanation: Correct: A, B, F. B: Create a single suggester with all three product name variant fields as source fields. F: Set the analyzer property on the product name fields for index-time tokenization, which is required for autocomplete to work. A: Query the autocomplete endpoint specifying the suggesterName. C: The search endpoint returns full results, not autocompletion suggestions. D: Only ONE suggester is needed with multiple source fields, not one per field. E: searchAnalyzer controls query-time analysis; the analyzer property (index-time) must be set for autocomplete source fields.

The financial documents are standardized PDFs and JPEGs with a distinct standard for each office. Which two API endpoints should you identify? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
questions.explanation: Correct: B and E. The financial documents have a distinct standard per office requiring a custom Form Recognizer model trained per layout. B: The custom model analyze endpoint submits documents for extraction using a trained custom model. E: The /vision/v3.1/read/analyze endpoint is the initial Read API call for asynchronous OCR text extraction from JPEG images. A: /vision/v3.1/read/analyzeResults is the polling endpoint to retrieve results, not an initial analysis endpoint. questions.questionText: You are developing the knowledgebase for Contoso using Azure Cognitive Search. Contoso needs to process wiki content to meet the technical requirements. All planned projects must support English, French, and Portuguese. Text-based content is provided only in one language and is not translated. What should you include in the solution?
options: A. an indexer for Azure Blob storage attached to a skillset that contains the language detection skill and the text translation skill
B. an indexer for Azure Blob storage attached to a skillset that contains the language detection skill
C. an indexer for Azure Cosmos DB attached to a skillset that contains the document extraction skill and the text translation skill

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Wiki content is stored as files in Azure Blob Storage. Since content is in one language but must support three languages, you need both the language detection skill (to identify source language) and the text translation skill (to translate to required languages). B: Language detection alone identifies the language but does not translate it, failing the multilingual requirement. C: Azure Cosmos DB is for structured data, not typical wiki file content; Blob Storage is correct. D: Cosmos DB indexer is incorrect for file-based wiki content.

questions.questionText: You are developing the knowledgebase for Contoso using Azure Cognitive Search. You need to meet the knowledgebase requirement for supporting searches for equivalent terms. What should you include in the solution?
options: D. a built-in key phrase extraction skill
questions.explanation: Correct: A. A synonym map. Azure Cognitive Search synonym maps define equivalent terms so a search for one term automatically expands to include its synonyms (e.g., searching 'car' also returns results for 'automobile'). This directly meets the requirement to support searches for equivalent terms. B: A suggester enables autocompletion as users type, not equivalent term mapping. C: A custom analyzer defines tokenization during indexing/querying, not synonym mapping. D: Key phrase extraction skill enriches documents during indexing but does not enable searching with equivalent terms at query time.

questions.questionText: You are developing a chatbot for Contoso. You create the following components: a QnA Maker resource and a chatbot by using the Azure Bot Framework SDK. You need to add an additional component to meet the technical requirements and the chatbot requirements including supporting multiple languages and providing other response options when confidence score is low. What should you add?
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Orchestrator. Bot Framework Orchestrator is a dispatch routing technology that routes incoming messages to the appropriate AI component (QnA Maker, LUIS, CLU, etc.). When multiple AI components exist, Orchestrator evaluates which component best handles each message and routes accordingly. This integrates existing components to meet the chatbot requirements. A: Microsoft Translator provides translation but does not integrate QnA Maker with the bot or route messages. B: Language Understanding (LUIS/CLU) provides intent recognition but the integration routing need points to Orchestrator. D: Chatdown is a prototyping tool for writing conversation mock-ups, not a production integration component.

questions.questionText: You are building a solution that needs to autonomously plan and execute multi-step tasks using built-in tools like code execution, file search, and custom functions — without requiring a predefined workflow graph. Which Azure service should you use?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Microsoft Foundry Agent Service is the managed service for creating AI agents that autonomously plan and execute multi-step tasks using built-in tools (code interpreter, file search) and custom function tools. The agent reasons about which tools to call without a predefined workflow.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Azure AI Bot Service builds conversational bots following defined dialog flows, not autonomous multi-step agents.
- C. Azure Logic Apps automates workflows with predefined connector steps, not AI-driven autonomous planning.
- D. Azure Durable Functions orchestrates code-based workflows defined by a developer, not AI-reasoned tool selection.

questions.questionText: You are creating an agent using Microsoft Foundry Agent Service. The agent must write and execute Python code to analyze uploaded CSV data and produce charts in response to user questions. Which built-in tool should you enable on the agent?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C. Code interpreter is a built-in tool in Microsoft Foundry Agent Service that lets the agent write and run Python code in a sandboxed environment, enabling data analysis and chart generation.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. File search indexes files and retrieves relevant passages but cannot execute code.
- B. Bing grounding lets the agent search the public web, not execute code.
- D. Azure Functions can be exposed as a custom tool but requires you to write and deploy the function yourself; it does not provide a built-in sandboxed Python environment.

questions.questionText: You are building an agent using Microsoft Foundry Agent Service that must answer questions about your organization's internal PDF documents stored in Azure Blob Storage. The agent should retrieve relevant passages from these documents before responding. Which built-in tool enables this capability?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C. File search is the built-in retrieval tool in Microsoft Foundry Agent Service that indexes your uploaded files and enables the agent to search them for relevant content at query time.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Code interpreter executes Python code in a sandbox; it does not perform semantic search over files.
- B. Bing grounding searches the public internet, not your private internal documents.
- D. Azure AI Search can be wired as a custom tool but requires additional development; file search is the native built-in option for this scenario.

msLearn.primaryTopic: File search tool in Azure AI Agent Service
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Foundry > Agent Service > Tools > File search

questions.questionText: When using Microsoft Foundry Agent Service, you have created an agent definition. You now want to process a user's message with that agent. Which two objects must you create at runtime to execute the agent against a user message? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
questions.explanation:
Correct: A. Thread and C. Run.

A Thread holds the conversation history (messages). A Run executes the agent on that thread, causing the agent to read the messages and decide what actions or responses to produce.

Why the others are wrong:
- B. Tool definitions are configured on the agent itself, not created per interaction.
- D. Session token is not a concept in the Foundry Agent Service API.
- E. Context window is an internal model concept, not an object you create in the agent API.

msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Foundry > Agent Service > Concepts > Threads and runs

questions.questionText: You are designing a complex AI solution where a coordinator agent breaks down user requests and delegates sub-tasks to specialized agents: a research agent, a writing agent, and a review agent. Each specialist agent returns results to the coordinator. What pattern does this represent?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Multi-agent orchestration. This describes a pattern where a coordinator/orchestrator agent delegates tasks to specialized sub-agents and aggregates their results, enabling complex workflows that exceed the capability of any single agent.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. RAG retrieves documents to ground model responses; it does not involve multiple collaborating agents.
- C. Prompt chaining passes output from one prompt as input to the next in a linear sequence; it does not involve autonomous agent delegation.
- D. Function calling allows a model to invoke specific tools/functions; it is a mechanism used within an agent, not the pattern describing multi-agent collaboration.

msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Foundry > Agent Service > Multi-agent

questions.questionText: You need to build an agentic solution that can adapt its plan based on intermediate results, autonomously retry failed steps, and manage long-running tasks without requiring you to predefine every workflow step in code. Which approach best meets these requirements?
options: A. Azure AI Foundry prompt flow
C. Azure Logic Apps with AI connectors
D. Azure Durable Functions with activity functions
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Microsoft Foundry Agent Service enables fully autonomous agents that dynamically plan, select tools, retry on failure, and manage long-running tasks — without requiring a predefined workflow graph.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Prompt flow requires you to define the flow graph (nodes and connections) in advance; it does not support dynamic AI-driven re-planning.
- C. Azure Logic Apps requires predefined connectors and steps; the workflow structure is fixed at design time.
- D. Azure Durable Functions requires developer-defined orchestration code; the control flow is not driven by AI reasoning.

questions.questionText: You are setting up Azure AI Foundry for a team of AI engineers who will work on multiple separate AI projects. You need a top-level resource that provides shared compute, connections, and storage that all projects can inherit. What should you create first?
options: D. An Azure Machine Learning workspace
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. An Azure AI hub is the top-level organizing resource in Azure AI Foundry. It provides shared infrastructure — compute, storage, connections, and governance — that multiple child projects inherit. Projects are created within a hub.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. An Azure AI project is created inside a hub; it cannot exist without one and does not provide shared infrastructure.
- C. An Azure OpenAI resource provides model endpoints but is not the Foundry organizational container.
- D. An Azure Machine Learning workspace is separate from AI Foundry and does not serve as a Foundry hub.

questions.questionText: You are building a generative AI solution that must answer questions about your company's proprietary product documentation. The model must not fabricate answers and must cite sources from your documents. The document set is updated weekly. Which pattern is most appropriate?
options: A. Fine-tuning the model on the documentation
C. Few-shot prompting with document excerpts
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) retrieves relevant document chunks at query time and includes them in the prompt, grounding the model in your data. This reduces hallucination, enables source citation, and handles weekly updates without retraining.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Fine-tuning updates model weights but doesn't support real-time document retrieval or source citation, and retraining weekly is expensive and slow.
- C. Few-shot prompting includes examples in the prompt but cannot scale to large document sets and doesn't retrieve relevant passages dynamically.
- D. System messages guide model behavior and tone but cannot provide access to document content or citation capabilities.

msLearn.primaryTopic: RAG pattern in Azure AI Foundry
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Foundry > Generative AI > RAG pattern

questions.questionText: In Azure AI Foundry prompt flow, you want to systematically measure the quality of your RAG solution by comparing model outputs against a ground truth dataset and computing metrics such as groundedness and relevance at scale. Which prompt flow type should you create?
options: D. Batch run on a standard flow
questions.explanation:
Correct: C. An evaluation flow is a special prompt flow type designed to assess the quality of other flows or model outputs. It takes inputs like model responses and ground truth, then produces quality metrics such as groundedness, relevance, fluency, and coherence.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. A standard flow processes data through a defined graph but does not produce evaluation metrics by default.
- B. A chat flow is optimized for multi-turn conversational experiences, not evaluation.
- D. A batch run executes a flow over multiple inputs but does not itself define evaluation logic; you need an evaluation flow for that.

msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Foundry > Prompt flow > Evaluation flows

questions.questionText: You are integrating Azure OpenAI into an e-commerce application. Users type a text description of a product they want to see, and the application generates a matching product image. Which Azure OpenAI model and API endpoint should you use?
options: A. GPT-4o with the chat completions endpoint
B. DALL-E with the image generation endpoint
C. GPT-4 Vision with the chat completions endpoint
D. text-embedding-ada-002 with the embeddings endpoint
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. DALL-E is Azure OpenAI's image generation model. You submit a text prompt to the /images/generations endpoint and receive a generated image.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. GPT-4o is a multimodal text and vision model that generates text, not images from scratch.
- C. GPT-4 Vision analyzes existing images and generates text descriptions; it does not create new images from text prompts.
- D. text-embedding-ada-002 converts text into vector embeddings for similarity search; it does not generate images.

msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > OpenAI > How-to > Image generation > DALL-E

questions.questionText: You need an Azure OpenAI model to consistently respond using your company's specific communication style, terminology, and structured output format across thousands of daily interactions. The style requirements are static and well-defined. Prompt token costs are a concern. Which approach is most appropriate?
options: A. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with a style guide document
B. Fine-tuning the model on examples of the required style
C. A detailed system message included in every request
D. Few-shot examples appended to every user message
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Fine-tuning trains the model on examples of the required style, baking the behavior into the model weights. This eliminates the need to include style instructions in every prompt, reducing token costs and providing more consistent results at scale.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. RAG retrieves documents to answer questions; it does not adapt the model's output style.
- C. System messages guide style but consume tokens on every request and are less reliable for strict style consistency at high scale.
- D. Few-shot examples consume significant tokens per request and are inconsistent — the wrong approach when token costs are a concern and requirements are static.

msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > OpenAI > How-to > Fine-tuning

questions.questionText: You are evaluating a RAG-based question answering solution in Azure AI Foundry. You need to measure whether the model's answers contain only information that is factually supported by the retrieved source documents, with no fabricated information added by the model. Which evaluation metric should you use?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C. Groundedness measures whether every claim in the model's response is supported by the retrieved context. A high groundedness score means the model is not hallucinating or adding information beyond what the sources provide.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Fluency assesses the linguistic quality and readability of the response, not its factual alignment with sources.
- B. Coherence measures whether the response is logically well-structured and consistent internally, not whether it matches source documents.
- D. Relevance measures whether the response addresses the user's question, but does not verify that each claim is backed by the retrieved documents.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Evaluation metrics for generative AI in Azure AI Foundry
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > AI Foundry > Evaluate > Built-in metrics

questions.questionText: You are working with Azure OpenAI GPT-4 and the model consistently gives incorrect answers to complex multi-step reasoning problems. You want to improve accuracy without fine-tuning or changing the model. Which prompt engineering technique should you apply?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Chain-of-thought prompting instructs the model to reason through intermediate steps before producing a final answer (e.g., adding 'Think step by step' to the prompt). This significantly improves accuracy on complex multi-step reasoning tasks.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Zero-shot prompting provides no examples or reasoning guidance; it would not improve multi-step reasoning accuracy.
- C. Reducing temperature makes outputs more deterministic but does not improve the quality of reasoning — a consistently wrong deterministic answer is still wrong.
- D. Increasing max_tokens allows longer responses but does not guide the model to reason correctly; it only prevents truncation.

msLearn.primaryTopic: Prompt engineering techniques for Azure OpenAI
msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > OpenAI > Concepts > Prompt engineering > Techniques

questions.questionText: Your production application requires consistent, predictable throughput from Azure OpenAI with guaranteed performance SLAs to handle a high and steady volume of requests. Which Azure OpenAI deployment type should you choose?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Provisioned throughput units (PTU) allocate dedicated model capacity for your deployment, providing guaranteed throughput and consistent latency with an SLA — ideal for steady high-volume production workloads.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Standard (pay-per-use) uses shared capacity across all Azure OpenAI customers. It can be throttled under high load and provides no throughput guarantee.
- C. Serverless API is used for models in the Azure AI model catalog (non-OpenAI models), not for Azure OpenAI deployments.
- D. Global batch is for asynchronous offline/batch processing with a 24-hour SLA, not real-time guaranteed throughput.

msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > OpenAI > Concepts > Deployment types > Provisioned

questions.questionText: You are building an application where users upload images of technical diagrams and ask natural language questions about them. The application must analyze the image content and respond with detailed text explanations. Which Azure OpenAI model should you use?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. GPT-4o is a large multimodal model that natively accepts both image and text inputs and generates text responses. It can analyze image content and answer questions about it.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. GPT-4 (text-only deployment) cannot process image inputs; it accepts only text.
- C. DALL-E 3 generates new images from text prompts; it cannot analyze an input image and answer questions.
- D. text-embedding-ada-002 converts text to vector embeddings for similarity search; it does not process images or generate text responses.

msLearn.navigationPath: Azure > OpenAI > How-to > GPT-4o > Vision

questions.questionText: You have implemented a RAG solution in Azure AI Foundry prompt flow. The flow retrieves relevant documents from Azure AI Search and passes them to a GPT model. During testing you notice the model frequently ignores the retrieved documents and answers from its own training knowledge. What is the most effective fix?
options: A. Increase the temperature parameter so the model is more creative with the context
B. Update the system message to instruct the model to answer only from the provided context, and to say 'I don't know' when the answer is not in the context
C. Retrieve more documents per query to increase the chance the answer is present
D. Switch to a larger model with more parameters
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. The system message must explicitly instruct the model to restrict its answers to the provided context and respond with 'I don't know' when the context doesn't contain the answer. Without this instruction, the model defaults to its parametric knowledge.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Higher temperature makes outputs more random; it does not cause the model to use retrieved context more faithfully.
- C. Retrieving more documents increases recall but doesn't prevent the model from ignoring the retrieved context in favour of its training knowledge.
- D. A larger model has the same default behaviour of using its parametric knowledge; without explicit instruction it will also ignore context.

questions.questionText: You are deploying an Azure OpenAI application and need to protect it from adversarial prompt inputs that attempt to override your system prompt instructions, bypass safety guardrails, or make the model ignore its configured behavior. Which Azure AI Content Safety feature should you enable?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Prompt shields in Azure AI Content Safety detect jailbreak attacks — adversarial inputs designed to override system prompts, bypass safety instructions, or manipulate the model into behaving against its guidelines.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Content filters detect and block harmful content categories (violence, hate, sexual, self-harm) but do not specifically detect jailbreak/prompt injection attacks.
- C. Blocklists filter specific words or phrases you define but cannot detect the semantic intent of a jailbreak attempt.
- D. Groundedness detection measures whether model responses are supported by retrieved source documents; it is not a jailbreak protection feature.

questions.questionText: You are deploying an Azure OpenAI model for a children's educational platform. You need to ensure all model inputs and outputs are automatically filtered for violent, sexual, hateful, and self-harm content at the strictest possible thresholds. Where do you configure this in Azure AI Foundry?
options: B. A content filters policy applied to the deployment
D. Azure Policy resource compliance assignments
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Content filters in Azure AI Foundry are configurable safety policies applied directly to model deployments. They automatically evaluate inputs and outputs against harm categories at configurable severity thresholds, blocking content that exceeds the threshold before it reaches users or the model.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Deployment parameters (temperature, max tokens, etc.) control model generation behaviour, not content safety filtering.
- C. System messages guide model behaviour but are not enforced safety controls — they can potentially be circumvented by adversarial inputs.
- D. Azure Policy governs Azure resource configuration and compliance; it does not perform content-level filtering on model inputs and outputs.

questions.topic: Plan and Manage an Azure AI Solution
questions.questionText: You are configuring Azure AI Content Safety for an Azure OpenAI deployment. The default content filter policy monitors inputs and outputs across four built-in harm categories. Which four categories does it cover? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
questions.explanation:
Correct: A. Hate, B. Violence, C. Sexual, D. Self-harm.

The four built-in harm categories in Azure AI Content Safety / Azure OpenAI content filters are:
- Hate: content that dehumanizes people based on identity characteristics
- Violence: content describing or promoting physical violence
- Sexual: sexually explicit or suggestive content
- Self-harm: content promoting or describing self-injury or suicide

Each category is assessed at four severity levels: safe, low, medium, and high.

Why the others are wrong:
- E. Spam is not one of the four standard harm categories.
- F. Misinformation is not one of the four standard harm categories; it is not currently a built-in content filter category.

questions.topic: Plan and Manage an Azure AI Solution
questions.questionText: Your organization is about to deploy multiple AI solutions and needs a formal process for identifying potential harms before release, assessing societal risks, documenting accountability, and ensuring AI decisions are auditable. Which Microsoft framework provides these guidelines?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B. The Microsoft Responsible AI Standard is a governance framework that provides requirements and guidance for building AI responsibly, including impact assessments, harm identification, accountability documentation, and oversight processes.

Why the others are wrong:
- A. Azure Policy enforces cloud resource configuration compliance (e.g., requiring encryption); it is not an AI ethics or governance framework.
- C. Azure Blueprints packages Azure resource deployments for compliance; it is not related to AI responsibility principles.
- D. The Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework provides broad cloud adoption strategy; it does not specifically address AI harm assessment or responsible AI governance.
